primitives.name: Shin Probability Inversion
primitives.verbatim_quote: Working form is the closed root used in the implied-probability literature: p_i(z) = (sqrt(z2 + 4(1-z) π_i2 / Σπ) - z) / (2(1-z)), z bisected so Σp = 1.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_i': 'implied probability of outcome i, dimensionless', 'z': 'risk-neutral parameter, dimensionless', 'π_i': 'prior probability of outcome i, dimensionless', 'Σπ': 'sum of prior probabilities, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Risk-neutral pricing assumption; bounded probability space; closed-form solution for inverse mapping.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When z approaches 1 or π_i becomes negligible, numerical instability arises.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Shin inversion primitive resolves a core issue in probability calibration by ensuring Σp = 1 through a closed-form root. It operates under risk-neutral pricing and is robust against degenerate cases where z→1. The Kalman rating system provides dynamic state estimation, enabling real-time adjustments to evolving game conditions. Market strength inversion ensures alignment between model predictions and market signals, using least squares optimization. These primitives interlock through shared game factors and probabilistic inversion, forming a coherent framework for predictive analytics in GSE and GSI.
